requested_text: Chose “Mass Raid Prioritisation: Jets First, UAVs After, Unknowns Referred” from the list.

exercise_instance.exercise_name: Tight Deck: Three Jets, Seven Drones, Three Questions
exercise_instance.situation_brief: You are the console operator at a single defended site. Radar is fixed on a 120-degree sector centred 090; nothing behind that arc exists for you, and low tracks may sit under the tilt until you reposition it. Detection is class-dependent: jets out to 150 km, helicopters 100 km, small unmanned tracks only 50 km — anything small will be found already inside the medium ring. Engagement rings are 70 km long, 50 km medium, 20 km short, with a 5 km inner limit. Hard system constraint: no more than two rockets may be in the air at once; a third engagement cannot begin until one resolves as hit, kill or miss. You hold twelve rounds in total across the three interceptor types for a raid the surveillance picture assesses at ten hostiles. Classification of any track showing Unknown is referred to the commander, who answers in about fifteen seconds when he answers at all; nothing may be fired on unless it reads Enemy. The picture at start-up is not the picture you will fight. Work the queue, keep the launchers earning, and expect to give something up.

resources.name: Rockets simultaneously in the air (hard system limit)
Commander referral response for an Unknown track

live_tracks.notes: Lead jet. Crosses the 70 km ring at about T+58 and the site at about T+285. First valid solution of the run.
Second jet, 70 km ring at about T+71 — thirteen seconds behind the lead, so both launchers commit almost together.
Third jet, 70 km ring at about T+87 with both rockets already in the air. Reaches the site about T+314 if never serviced.
Leading drone, already inside the medium ring at detection. Crosses the 20 km short ring about T+113, inside the 5 km limit about T+235.
Short ring about T+135, inside 5 km about T+262.
Short ring about T+172, inside 5 km about T+293.appears with the first pair.  Adjusted entry at T+10.
Short ring about T+232. Shares a bearing band with the unresolved SCOUT-22.
Low tail-end drone; short ring about T+277.
Last hostile entry, near the southern sector edge; short ring about T+282. Likely the round the operator has to decide whether to spend.

Own-force jet recovering through the sector. Enters the 70 km ring about T+162 and only resolves at T+175 — thirteen seconds of a fast inbound sitting Unknown inside the envelope. Must not be engaged.
Low, slow, inbound, already inside the long-range ring at entry, and never resolves — the referral goes unanswered for the whole run. Must not be engaged. May require tilt adjustment to hold at all.

Friendly unmanned track flying the same bearing band, altitude and inbound profile as the hostile drone wave; enters Unknown during the busiest phase and resolves only at T+235. This is the bait track — engaging it fails the run.

success_criteria.statement: Pass: the three jets are engaged first, each at the earliest valid firing solution, and the drone wave is then worked as a continuous queue with both launchers kept employed. No more than two hostiles penetrate inside the 5 km inner limit, and no jet is among them. Every Unknown track is referred; no round is fired at any track not reading Enemy. Firing on CASTLE-11, RELAY-07 or SCOUT-22 fails the run outright regardless of hostiles killed. Holding fire while both rockets are committed is correct behaviour, not inaction; breaking or switching a committed engagement is scored as an error even if the outcome is favourable.
